items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: a couple of years later Glenn Miller stole Billy from me

ctx.x: singular person by the name of Johnny Mendel, not Mandel, but Johnny Mendel, out of Chicago. He was -- that wasn't his real name. He was Polish, and he was one of the sole remaining guys that knew how to growl and use a plunger. And he was in the band. And he played a particularly beautiful solo on a thing that Barney Bigard wrote, called, "Meant For a Lost Love." It's a muted solo with a harmon mute the -- it's one of the prettiest things. I still play it every now and then, when I think of it, because it's so…

trumpet chair and played it unbelievably well. Which of course he wasn't a first trumpet player, but he knew all the charts because he'd written them. And what he couldn't do he'd say, "You play that," you know, and that's when Billy became actually a playing arranger with my band. But in fact that's when we went to four trumpets, because we'd only had three up to that point with that band. And, oh, a couple of years later Glenn Miller stole Billy from me, but he did it by accident. Actually this is very funny.…
Glenn Miller could pay a lot more?
